name: Connecticut
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+, with licensed adult-use sales since January 2023.
summary: Connecticut legalized adult-use cannabis through SB 1201, signed June 22, 2021, with possession legal from July 1, 2021 and retail sales starting January 10, 2023. Adults 21+ may carry 1.5 ounces and keep up to 5 ounces at home, and since July 2023 all adults may grow a small number of plants. In 2026 lawmakers replaced the THC-based cannabis tax with a flat 10.75% tax from October 1, 2026, and passed a broad cannabis and hemp law (Public Act 26-8) that also opens the medical market to qualifying out-of-state patients.

adult_use_since.value: Gov. Ned Lamont signed SB 1201 on June 22, 2021; adult possession became legal July 1, 2021.

possession_limit.value: Up to 1.5 ounces on your person, and up to 5 ounces at home or locked in a car's trunk or glove box.

home_grow.value: Since July 1, 2023, adults 21+ may grow up to 3 mature and 3 immature plants indoors in a locked area out of public view, with a household cap of 12 plants.

public_use.value: Smoking in public is generally not allowed, and smoking in a vehicle or driving while impaired is prohibited.

retail_sales.value: Licensed adult-use retail sales began Jan. 10, 2023.

taxes.value: From Oct. 1, 2026, a flat 10.75% cannabis tax on gross receipts replaces the former THC-per-milligram tax (Public Act 26-68). Adult-use buyers also pay the 3% municipal cannabis tax and state sales tax; registered medical patients are exempt.

medical_program.value: Patients certified by a provider for a qualifying condition register with the Department of Consumer Protection and buy tax-free. Public Act 26-8 (2026) lets qualifying out-of-state patients use the medical market starting Oct. 1, 2026.

regulator.value: Department of Consumer Protection (DCP), with the Social Equity Council overseeing equity licensing.

hemp_thc.value: Public Act 26-8 (HB 5350, signed May 20, 2026) tightens rules on hemp-derived and manufactured cannabinoids effective Dec. 1, 2026, and raises allowable THC in infused beverages from Oct. 1, 2026.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Connecticut's DUI law does not depend on a THC level, and driving under the influence of cannabis carries the same penalties as drunk driving. Cannabis may be transported in a locked glove box or trunk.

tourists.value: Yes. Any adult 21+ with a valid government photo ID can buy at adult-use or hybrid retailers regardless of residency, with the same 1.5-ounce possession limit and taxes as residents.

timeline.event: Gov. Ned Lamont signs SB 1201 legalizing adult-use cannabis
Home cultivation opens to all adults 21+

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can possess cannabis and buy it from licensed retailers, which have sold to adults since January 2023.

faq.q: How much weed can you have in Connecticut?
faq.a: Up to 1.5 ounces on your person and up to 5 ounces at home or locked in your car's trunk or glove box.

faq.q: Can you grow weed at home in Connecticut?
faq.a: Yes. Since July 2023 adults may grow three mature and three immature plants indoors in a locked space, with no more than 12 plants per household.

faq.q: What is the cannabis tax in Connecticut?
faq.a: Since Oct. 1, 2026 the state charges a flat 10.75% cannabis tax plus a 3% municipal tax and sales tax. Registered medical patients do not pay these taxes.

faq.q: Can out-of-state medical patients buy cannabis in Connecticut?
faq.a: A 2026 law (Public Act 26-8) allows qualifying out-of-state patients and caregivers to use Connecticut's medical market starting Oct. 1, 2026.
